bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Legislative Council polls: 8 seats, 164 candidates; stage set for multi-cornered battle
bihar_raw_news.content: PTI Patna: Jan Suraaj Party chief Prashant Kishor at an election campaign meeting ahead of the Bihar Legislative Council polls. Bihar's eight-seat Legislative Council contest has drawn 164 candidates, setting the stage for a multi-cornered electoral battle ahead of the October 23 polls. The office of the state's Chief Electoral Officer said 98 candidates have entered the race across four graduates' constituencies, while another 66 have filed papers for four teachers' seats. Tuesday was the final day for submitting nominations. The seats going to the polls are Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi Graduates' constituencies, along with Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran Teachers' constituencies. Darbhanga Graduates' constituency has attracted the largest field among the four graduates' seats, with 40 candidates. Patna has 22 nominees, while Tirhut and Kosi have 20 and 16, respectively. Also read | Election Commission rejects Rahul Gandhi-led MPs' meeting request amid SIR row, says 2025 procedure must be followed Live Events Among teachers' constituencies, Patna has recorded 22 candidates. Saran follows with 19, while Darbhanga and Tirhut have 14 and 11 candidates, respectively. The next stage of the election process will begin with scrutiny of nomination papers on October 7. Candidates have until October 9 to withdraw from the contest. Voting is scheduled between 8 am and 4 pm on October 23. The counting of votes will take place on October 27. The election has significance for the eight sitting MLCs whose terms end on November 16. They are Neeraj Kumar from Patna Graduates, Sarvesh Kumar from Darbhanga Graduates, Bansi Dhar Brajwasi from Tirhut Graduates, N K Yadav from Kosi Graduates, Naval Kishore Yadav from Patna Teachers, Madan Mohan Jha from Darbhanga Teachers, Sanjay Kumar Singh from Tirhut Teachers and Afaque Ahmad from Saran Teachers. The BJP has nominated four candidates and the JD(U) has candidates in the other four constituencies. Among the BJP nominees are three sitting MLCs seeking another term — Nawal Kishor Yadav from Patna Teachers, Dr N K Yadav from Kosi Graduates and Sarvesh Kumar from Tirhut Graduates. Also read | Uttar Pradesh: Eight BJP candidates file nominations in Lucknow for upcoming Rajya Sabha polls The BJP has also nominated Narendra Kumar Singh in Tirhut Teachers' constituency. The seat is currently represented by CPI's Sanjay Kumar Singh, whose party is part of the opposition INDIA bloc. The Jan Suraaj Party, led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting every one of the eight constituencies. Its candidates include Anuj Singh from Patna Graduates, Vimohan Kumar from Tirhut Graduates, Shyam Nandan Yadav from Tirhut Teachers and Afaq Ahmed from Saran Teachers. Divya Jyoti, a lawyer and academician-turned-politician, is contesting from Patna Teachers. The party has fielded S P Rai from Darbhanga Teachers, Mohammad Imtiyaz from Darbhanga Graduates and Rajnish Ranjan from Kosi Graduates. The electorate for graduates' constituencies is made up of eligible graduates residing in the respective constituencies. They must have obtained a degree from a recognised university in India and separately enrolled themselves on the relevant electoral roll. Teachers' constituencies have a different eligibility criterion.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary reviews flood situation, directs officials to submit detailed ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary reviews flood situation, directs officials to submit detailed damage report ANI | Updated: Oct 06, 2026 21:48 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], October 6 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary reviewed the flood situation in the state and the damage caused by it, directing officials to submit a detailed report at the earliest. According to a press release, the review meeting was held at the 'Sankalp' auditorium at Lok Sevak Awas in the presence of BJP national president and MP Nitin Nabin. During the meeting on Tuesday, Water Resources Department Secretary Dr Chandrashekhar Singh briefed the Chief Minister about the causes of the floods and the situation that emerged in the state in two phases. During the first phase, the Ganga, Son, Ghaghra, Kosi and Punpun rivers recorded new highest water levels compared to previous records. In the second phase, the Gandak River recorded its highest water levels at four locations due to excessive rainfall. Six locations in West Champaran, Gopalganj and Saran districts witnessed damage to embankments. Disaster Management Department Principal Secretary Santosh Kumar Mall briefed the meeting about the relief and rescue operations carried out during the floods. Choudhary said a serious flood situation emerged this year due to the exceptionally high volume of water in the Ganga, Gandak and Son rivers compared to previous years. He said accumulation of silt in riverbeds was also one of the major reasons for floods. Bihar is the first state in the country to formulate a silt policy, the Chief Minister said. The CM directed officials to continuously monitor the current condition of rivers and the damage caused by the floods and directed that a preliminary detailed report on the damage caused by the floods be submitted at the earliest so that relief, rehabilitation and necessary development works in affected areas could be expedited. Choudhary said ex-gratia relief would be distributed among families affected by the second phase of floods on October 12, 2026. He also directed the Disaster Management Department to coordinate with all concerned departments to assess the damage caused by the floods and the expenditure likely to be incurred on restoration, and submit the report at the earliest. Officials were further directed to ensure necessary arrangements after the drainage of water from flood-affected areas, keeping in view possible problems that may arise. Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Disaster Management Minister Ratnesh Sada, Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Agriculture Department Principal Secretary Narmadeshwar Lal and other senior officials were present at the meeting. Meanwhile, CM Samrat Choudhary on Saturday (3 October) directed the Disaster Management Department to ensure timely delivery of relief materials to flood-affected and inaccessible areas of Saran district, with special air-dropping operations being carried out in coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Defence. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Muzaffarpur plans CBG plant to convert waste into clean energy under Cities 2.0
bihar_raw_news.content: Home All News Biogas (CBG) Bihar: Muzaffarpur plans CBG plant to convert waste into clean energy under... All News Biogas (CBG) Bihar: Muzaffarpur plans CBG plant to convert waste into clean energy under Cities 2.0 By BioEnergyTimes October 6, 2026 Muzaffarpur: Muzaffarpur is preparing to set up a compressed biogas (CBG) plant to convert city waste into useful energy under the Cities 2.0 project, as part of efforts to strengthen solid waste management and promote resource recovery, Amar Ujala reported. The project envisages establishing a Material Recovery Facility and a CBG plant in the city. The proposed system will focus on collecting and segregating waste at source, recovering useful materials and converting suitable waste into energy. An international delegation from Germany and France visited Muzaffarpur on Monday to review the proposed project and assess the scope for implementing the planned waste management and CBG facilities. The delegation discussed the feasibility of the proposed facilities and ways to maximise the use of waste generated in the city. The delegation is scheduled to visit the dumping yard at Rautiniya in Marwan block and other proposed sites on Tuesday. The team will assess the existing conditions, available resources and the possibility of implementing the proposed technology at these locations. The project also proposes the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to monitor sanitation and solid waste management activities. The system is expected to make monitoring more organised and technology-driven. The meeting also discussed promoting recycling and developing selected locations in Muzaffarpur as clean and attractive model spots. Officials said the proposed initiatives could make the city’s waste management system more effective and environmentally friendly. Municipal Commissioner Rituraj Pratap Singh gave a presentation on the Cities 2.0 project and the proposed activities. Officials from the Muzaffarpur Municipal Corporation and representatives of the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA) also attended the meeting. The international delegation included FD team head Fabrice Juqua, Antoine Mogenot, Justin Plorde Dehaumont, Nitesh Chandrakar and Amit Goswami. From NIUA, Saurabh Manuja, Mohammad Arif, Dilshad Ahmad and Puneet Babbar were present. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna Ring Road Corridor Targeted for 2028 Completion - RAHSTA Expo 2026
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna Ring Road Corridor Targeted for 2028 Completion Infrastructure Transport Oct 06 2026 The Bihar Road Construction Department has set 2028 as the completion target for the 14.5-km Ramnagar-Kachchi Dargah six-lane corridor, being developed as part of the Patna Ring Road network. The project has an estimated cost of Rs. 11.83 bn and is intended to strengthen connectivity around the city. Road Construction Department Secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal reviewed the project’s progress on Tuesday and instructed officials to keep construction on schedule. Engineers involved in the work discussed construction-related issues and measures needed to advance the corridor within the stipulated timeline. The section is being developed under NH-131G through the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) mode. It is designed to provide an alternative route for traffic moving through Patna and reduce dependence on roads passing through more congested parts of the city. The review also covered several other major road projects in Bihar. These included the Chausa-Buxar bypass, the Daudnagar bypass in Aurangabad, the four-lane road from Bhagalpur to Dhaka Mor and the Arwal bypass on NH-139. Officials further examined the proposed four-lane road connecting the Bihar-Jharkhand border with Bhaljore in Banka. The department discussed approval-related matters and progress updates for the Bettiah bypass on NH-727, along with the Madhepura and Singheshwar bypass projects on NH-131. Special Secretary Dr Shailaja Sharma and other project engineers attended the meeting. The department directed teams to accelerate construction and complete the schemes within their approved schedules, with the Ramnagar-Kachchi Dargah corridor forming a key part of Patna’s peripheral road network. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar bans DJs during Durga Puja, sets procession rules | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: October 06, 2026 Bihar bans DJs during Durga Puja, issues security rules for pandals and processions Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Bihar government has banned DJs during Durga Puja and Dasara and ordered tighter security at pandals, processions and immersion sites across the state. Officials have also issued rules for licences, crowd control and emergency arrangements. The decision followed a meeting on Monday chaired by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit and Director General of Police Preeta Verma. Divisional commissioners, district magistrates and superintendents of police attended the meeting. The rules will apply across Bihar’s 40 districts, including 38 administrative districts and two police districts. Special administrative and security arrangements have been ordered from October 11 to 20, The Hindu reported. Licences, monitoring and crowd safety Licences are compulsory for puja pandals, idols and immersion processions, according to a Cabinet Secretariat department statement reported by PTI. Organisers must obtain undertakings from 10 to 25 responsible people participating in each procession. Authorities will photograph and record procession routes. Provocative songs, objectionable slogans, prohibited weapons and displays that could hurt community sentiments will not be allowed. Loudspeakers will require permission and cannot operate between 10 pm and 6 am. DJ operators and loudspeaker owners must register with sub-divisional authorities, while local police stations must maintain their details. Police have been directed to deploy personnel at sensitive locations and monitor social media. Large pandals will undergo fire safety audits by district fire officers. Officials have also ordered separate entry and exit points at crowded venues. Medical teams, ambulances, Quick Response Teams, State Disaster Response Force personnel, CCTV cameras and watchtowers must be available where required. Divers and rescue teams will be stationed at designated immersion ghats and Ravan Dahan sites. The government has asked officials to prioritise the safety of women and children. Additional restrictions in Barh The Barh subdivision administration in Patna district has announced additional rules for local puja committees. The directions followed a peace committee meeting held on Monday, Dainik Jagran reported. Pandals in the subdivision cannot exceed 40 feet, while Durga idols are limited to 20 feet. Organisers have also been barred from using plaster of Paris and chemical colours to make idols. Idols cannot be immersed in the Ganga within the subdivision. The Barh Nagar Parishad will instead create artificial ponds for immersion, according to the report. Local organisers must install CCTV cameras that operate throughout the day and deploy volunteers carrying identity cards. Pandals must also have help desks and separate waste bins. Committees must obtain a puja licence from the relevant police station and permission for loudspeakers from the sub-divisional office. Temporary electricity connections, covered wiring and miniature circuit breakers are compulsory where power is used. The local administration also directed organisers to keep pandals at least four feet away from electricity supply lines. The distance is intended to reduce the risk of electrical accidents. bihar_raw_news.title: India From digital to AI public infrastructure | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: October 06, 2026 India: From digital to AI public infrastructure Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Rajesh Seth India may be preparing for its next big digital leap. And this time, it could be about putting intelligence on top of the digital infrastructure that already exists. On September 21, Rajiv Kumar, President and Managing Director of Microsoft India, said India is on a roadmap to move from Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to AI public infrastructure over the next five years. He specifically referred to Aadhaar, UPI and Digi Yatra as examples of the country’s successful DPI. The statement raises a simple question: what exactly is AI public infrastructure? To understand this, think of India’s DPI as a network of digital highways. Aadhaar provides a digital identity. UPI provides a common rail for digital payments. Digi Locker provides a way to access digital documents. These are not individual services competing with private companies. They are common infrastructure on which thousands of public and private services can be built. Adding an intelligent layer AI public infrastructure could add an intelligent layer to these digital highways. Instead of simply enabling a transaction, an AI-enabled system could understand a person’s language, analyse information, personalise a service or help the person navigate a complicated process. In simple terms, DPI connects people digitally; AI infrastructure could help technology understand and assist them. This idea is not entirely theoretical. At the India AI Impact Summit in February, Nandan Nilekani, one of the architects of India’s digital public infrastructure, argued that the important question is how quickly AI can be productively diffused among people. Drawing a parallel with UPI, he said open networks allow many innovators to build applications using AI. He also argued that AI agents could remove complexity for users by allowing them to interact in their own language. That is an important distinction. India does not necessarily need to build every AI application itself. Just as UPI created an open architecture on which banks and technology companies could build payment services, an AI-enabled public infrastructure could allow many organisations to build applications for healthcare, agriculture, education and public services. The Singapore model Singapore provides an interesting glimpse of how such an approach can work. Its Government Technology Agency says it is building shared AI tools and data infrastructure for Government agencies. These include AI-powered citizen-service chatbots, productivity tools for public officers and analytics platforms. Instead of every agency developing its own AI system from scratch, shared infrastructure can reduce duplication and speed up deployment. Singapore’s updated National AI Strategy, released in May this year, also calls for AI to be embedded more deeply across Government to improve public services. But there is an important lesson here for India: AI infrastructure is not simply about computers and data centres. The World Bank’s latest research, based on Government responses from 60 economies, shows that AI adoption in Governments is already widespread but often shallow. national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said India needs a strong and integrated maritime ecosystem to further enhance its maritime power and strengthen the country’s defence capabilities. The Defence Minister today launched Fleet Support Ship-1, laid the keel for Fleet Support Ship-5 and inaugurated the upgraded Slipway-4 and a 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited in Visakhapatnam. Addressing the gathering, Mr Singh said the launch of Fleet Support Ship-1, keel laying of Fleet Support Ship-5 and inauguration of upgraded infrastructure at HSL mark important steps in strengthening India’s maritime capabilities. He said Fleet Support Ship-1, named ‘Surya’, will strengthen the Indian Navy’s reach, endurance and operational effectiveness. He said the new slipway and Goliath crane at HSL will further enhance the shipyard’s capacity to undertake large shipbuilding projects. The Defence Minister said the Indian Navy has repeatedly demonstrated its capabilities in the Indian Ocean Region as a first responder and preferred security partner. He said the Navy has played an important role in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, anti-piracy operations, evacuation missions and maritime security. Mr Singh said, Hindustan Shipyard Limited has played an important role in meeting India’s maritime and defence requirements for more than eight decades. He said the shipyard’s Miniratna Category-I status, accorded in 2025, reflects its transformation and improved financial position. The Defence Minister said the Navy, shipyards, DRDO, academia, industry, MSMEs and start-ups need to work together as an integrated team to build a strong national maritime ecosystem. Mr Singh said India has immense potential in shipbuilding, but the challenge is to convert this potential into capability and global competitiveness. He stressed the need to focus on timely delivery, productivity, indigenous design capability, resilient supply chains, skilled manpower, capacity expansion and cost competitiveness. He said India’s defence manufacturing sector has undergone significant transformation over the past decade, with the country moving from dependence on imported platforms towards designing and manufacturing advanced systems and platforms domestically. Mr Singh said India aims to become a developed nation by 2047, with a self-reliant, secure and prosperous economy and a respected position in the world.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 87 eSanjeevani crosses 50 crore teleconsultations, marking milestone in India’s digital healthcare i...
national_raw_news.content: India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations, marking a significant milestone in the Government’s efforts to leverage digital technology to make quality healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable for citizens across the country. The platform recorded over 50 crore teleconsultations cumulatively across all States and Union Territories. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said that the achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas. eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of the country’s digital health ecosystem and as the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare. Further, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live. The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. The initiative currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, over 19 thousand medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with over two lakh registered healthcare providers. The platform is facilitating around 2.5 to 3 lakh consultations every day in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages. Its highest single-day utilisation has crossed six lakh consultations. Women account for over 57 per cent of total utilisation, while 40 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above. The platform has evolved with the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare. eSanjeevani is now expanding to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna. eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.

national_raw_news.title: Centre approves Rs 10,000 crore fund for equity capital of SME as FTAs open expansion ...
national_raw_news.content: Centre approves Rs 10,000 crore fund for equity capital of SME as FTAs open expansion opportunities Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Centre approves Rs 10,000 crore fund for equity capital of SME as FTAs open expansion opportunities ANI | Updated: Oct 06, 2026 16:09 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 6 (ANI): The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved a government commitment of Rs 10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund, aimed at providing direct equity investments to growth-oriented small and medium enterprises and helping create a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing globally. The fund is expected to address a structural gap in long-term growth capital available to SMEs, particularly enterprises seeking to scale operations, adopt advanced technologies, expand internationally and integrate into global value chains, according to a release. Briefing the media, Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting, Ashwini Vaishnaw said the new fund for SME’s was established keeping in mind the plethora of opportunities expected to be unlocked due to the recent Free Trade Agreements with countries such as New Zealand, Australia, UAE, UK and more. “The growth fund is aimed at long term funding for SME’s….more than half of the fund will go to manufacturing-focused MSMEs,” said Vishnaw. The SME Growth Fund is aimed at providing “patient growth equity capital” to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. A majority of the fund's allocation will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing-focused enterprises, while SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities will also be considered. Under the initiative, the government will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund established under the SME Growth Fund framework. The fund is expected to support SMEs at critical stages of expansion by enabling them to increase manufacturing capacity, invest in technology, undertake strategic investments and access international markets. The government expects the initiative to accelerate the creation of a pipeline of Indian companies with greater scale, innovation capabilities and competitiveness. The move comes as the government seeks to strengthen the SME ecosystem beyond traditional credit support. According to the release, while various initiatives have improved access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required for scaling, innovation, acquisitions and transformation into industry leaders. The fund will also focus on industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, with the government expecting investments in these regions to support balanced industrial development, strengthen local supply chains and generate quality employment. The initiative is also expected to improve productivity and export competitiveness of manufacturing enterprises as they gain access to capital for capacity expansion and advanced technology adoption. The SME Growth Fund will complement existing government measures covering digitalisation, credit support, ease of doing business, public procurement, startup promotion and production-linked incentive programmes. national_raw_news.content: Best performing states, UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY 2.0 felicitated at World Habitat Day celebrations Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Best performing states, UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY 2.0 felicitated at World Habitat Day celebrations ANI | Updated: Oct 05, 2026 23:56 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 5 (ANI): The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs ( MoHUA ) celebrated World Habitat Day 2026 on the theme ‘Adequate Housing for All’ with a focus on strengthening the urban housing ecosystem through innovation, policy reforms, technology and sustainable financing. Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs Tokhan Sahu was the guest of honour of the event. Representatives of UN-Habitat, senior officials from Ministry, Principal Secretaries from States and Union Territories and other stakeholders also attended the event, marked by participation of UN agencies, HUDCO, NHB among others. The celebration provided a platform to highlight India’s continued efforts towards ensuring access to safe, affordable, inclusive and dignified housing, while recognising the contributions of States/UTs and other stakeholders towards achieving the objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-U 2.0, a release said. The event showcased the progress and diverse approaches being adopted towards achieving the objective of “Housing for All”, including best practices under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0. As part of the PMAY-U Awards 2026, Best Performing States/UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 were felicitated, along with ULBs, partner agencies/stakeholders recognising their performance in implementing housing initiatives, including rental housing.
